Resolves #21135

A changed cell in an `animatedChange` column keeps its mark when its row is rebuilt, and every change restarts its animation. Until now the mark lived only in a class patched into the row's vdom 20 ms after the change, so a forced view pass that rebuilt the row before the patch was sent dropped it. That is the intermittent StoreUpdateRowsNL red on `dev` and on PRs.

The mark is now render state:
- The column keeps each changed record's classes for `markDuration` (1 s, longer than the 0.4 s animation). `Neo.grid.Row#applyRendererOutput` adds them through an optional `getCellStateCls(rendererConfig)` hook on every render.
- The column hears a change ahead of the grid bodies (`order: 'before'`), so the body's own repaint renders the mark: a single edit's row render, or a store batch's one repaint. The column patches no cell and updates no row.
- A new mark adds `neo-animated-alt` when the cell as last rendered carries the same classes without it: a live mark, or an ended one that no render took off yet. Its duplicate keyframes restart the animation. A cell carrying both gets the plain classes again.
- Marks are inserted last, so the map holds them in the order they end. Each mark visits the head, and an ended mark is visited once when it leaves.
- `AnimatedCurrency` keeps its sign classes and gains the same `-alt` keyframes.

Evidence: L3 (real Chromium on the big-data grid example: `animationstart` events on a counter cell, and the batch repaint's flight held while a forced view pass rebuilds the rows) → L3 required (AC-2 and AC-3 are browser behavior). No residuals.

## Deltas from ticket

- **The hook.** #21135 first named `Column.Base#getCellCls`, and the body now names what shipped: an optional `column.getCellStateCls?.()` that `Row` reads after the `cellCls` config. `RowCellIdMigration.spec` and `TreeRowAria.spec` build rows from duck-typed plain-object columns, so a required method on every column broke them. `Column.Base` stays as it is.
- **A store that keys its records** is now part of AnimatedChange's contract. `NestedDataField.spec`'s stub store gains `getKey`.
- **The cost of the marks.** A store batch of 5,000 hydrated records stays within 10,000 visits to mark entries in the unit control. `318b2aad` made 12,469,604.
- **The offscreen-column alias** from @neo-gpt-emmy's defect note: with no patch, an edit to a column without rendered cells no longer reaches another column's pooled slot. A unit arm edits c23 of a 24-column grid with four mounted slots: `318b2aad` marks c3, this head marks nothing. `Neo.grid.Body#getCellId`'s fallback is unchanged for its other callers.

## Test Evidence

- **Red first:**

  - at this head, with the two mutations @neo-gpt-emmy named: the forced-pass arm fails when the pass is never induced (the flight is not held) and when the forced rebuild drops the mark (`[false, false, false]` in the settled DOM).

- The dev themes built from this branch, and the compiled `AnimatedChange.css` carries `grid-animated-cell-alt`.

### 🔬 Depth Floor

**Visible behavior.** I compared base `56353531` with this head in headless Chrome using the BigData grid, the respective Row/AnimatedChange modules and compiled animation CSS. On the same stationary DOM cell I set the counter to 881, waited 1.3 seconds (the default mark lasts 1 second), set 882, then set 883 inside the new window. All three text updates appeared. The base emitted **three** native `animationstart` events; the candidate emitted **two**. At 882 the old `neo-animated` class was still painted. Expiry discarded the remembered phase, and the new mark selected the same CSS animation name. At 883 the alternate name started correctly. The unit expiry test forces a redraw before its assertion, which removes the stale class and misses this sequence. [Mark selection](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/318b2aad460bd667ca8ad89b1ca94d40be1430ae/src/grid/column/AnimatedChange.mjs#L102-L139)

**Batch cost.** In a Node fixture with the actual Store and subscribed column, I hydrated each row, held the clock inside the mark window, and sent one `store.updateRows` batch. At 256 / 1,000 / 5,000 distinct changed records the cleanup callback visited **0 / 467,604 / 12,469,604** entries. Each run emitted one `rowsChange` and returned zero errors. Every mark after the 256th scans the entire live map, even when nothing can expire. Counting row updates alone misses this worker cost. [Cleanup loop](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/318b2aad460bd667ca8ad89b1ca94d40be1430ae/src/grid/column/AnimatedChange.mjs#L136-L139)

**Inherited behavior, separate from the verdict.** A 24-column grid with four mounted cell slots can flash the wrong column on a single offscreen edit: changing c23 patched visible c3 at the same modulo slot. Both the base and this head reproduce it. The direct patch should eventually check the bound row record and actual data field before decorating the pooled node. I’m recording this separately from the three required actions. [Direct patch](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/318b2aad460bd667ca8ad89b1ca94d40be1430ae/src/grid/column/AnimatedChange.mjs#L141-L150)

### 🧠 Graph Ingestion Notes

Store emits the prepared records’ changes before the batch notification. The column can therefore supply state when Row renders a mounted cell. Retention, expiry and restart are column concerns; the batch should keep its single body repaint.
